title: Word Problems Within 1,000
intro: Help your student recognize familiar story structures when the numbers get larger.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Have the student describe the action before calculating. Use hundreds, tens, and ones only after agreeing on an equation.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Already there: 468 counters.

Added: 257 counters.

468 + 257 = 725

Add 200 to get 668, add 50 to get 718, and add 7 to get 725.

703 − 268 = 435
435 + 268 = 703

A place-value method rewrites 703 as six hundreds, nine tens, and thirteen ones before subtracting.

Hundreds
100100100100100100

6 × 100 = 600

Tens
101010101010101010

9 × 10 = 90

Ones
1111111111111

13 × 1 = 13

600 + 90 + 13 = 703

Remove 2 hundreds, 6 tens, and 8 ones. That leaves 4 hundreds, 3 tens, and 5 ones: 435.

Ask your student

Would we use the same operation if the numbers were smaller?

If your student needs help

If large numbers distract from the story, discuss a smaller example with the same relationship first.
